title: The Next Challengers In Memory Chips

The Next Challengers In Memory Chips

Tilly Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 29 Jul 2026

The global shortage of memory chips brought by the artificial-intelligence boom has accelerated China’s ambitions in the sector. Two state-backed national champions have burned through a decade of losses as they built capacity and capability in the capital-intensive business. With demand and prices surging, their trajectory toward commercial viability has suddenly shifted. Now, CXMT Corp., the DRAM specialist, is massively profitable and one of China’s largest companies by market capitalization after its listing on the Shanghai STAR market. The smaller but more technically advanced flash-memory specialist, Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp., has also started preparations for an IPO.The opportunity for China to seize a larger share of the global market for memory chips is real. Demand is so strong that the major incumbents—Samsung and SK Hynix of South Korea, and Micron of the US—cannot expand production fast enough. Customers are thus becoming more willing to try new suppliers and more tolerant of any shortcomings in quality and stability. Memory chips are more standardized than other semiconductors and require less customer adaptation and testing, making entry of new competitors easier. Furthermore, the products that CXMT and YMTC are selling are less affected by the US export controls that have blocked China’s access to high-end chip-manufacturing equipment, making catch-up in memory more practical. The test will be whether these companies can use the current once-in-a-lifetime boom to build businesses that will survive the inevitable turn in the cycle.
